issue.title: Linux sandbox prevents action childs from writing files

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request / question:

When spawning child processes from within actions, these child processes do not have the same write rights the action process has.
E.g. when trying to write a file it works fine from the action process but fails in a child process.


### If possible, provide a minimal example to reproduce the problem:

    import multiprocess
    def _write_file(name):
        with open(name, "w") as file: # Fails with read only filesystem error
            file.write("FOO")
    def main():
        files = ["a", "b"]
        with open("c", "w") as file:
            file.write("FOO")
        with multiprocess.Pool() as pool:
            pool.map(_write_file, files)
    if __name__ == "__main__":
	main()


### Environment info
* Operating System: Ubuntu 16.04.2
* Bazel version (output of `bazel info release`): 0.4.3


###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web? (e.g. GitHub issues, email threads in the [bazel-discuss@googlegroups.com](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/bazel-discuss) archive)

milestone.title: Functional
milestone.description:
The rules __can__ be used to build dotnet code, but the rules require manual setup, reading of the documentation, and understanding bazelisms in order to use.

People who use bazel would be familiar with the rules, but people who use msbuild would not be familiar with the rules. 

Getting someone from the msbuild world to adopt the rules given only this milestone is accomplished would be difficult.
